questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 5]

The following diagram shows a solid hemisphere with centre A(6, -1, -3).
Point B(4, -5, -9) lies on the curved surface.

[Diagram: Solid hemisphere resting on a horizontal surface. Centre A is at the centre of the flat circular face. Point B is on the curved surface. A straight line segment AB is drawn from A to B, representing the radius of the hemisphere.]

(a) Find AB, the radius of the hemisphere. [2]

(b) Hence, find the total surface area of the solid hemisphere. [3]
questions.summary: Find the radius of a hemisphere in 3D coordinates and its total surface area.
questions.solution: (a) AB = √((6-4)² + (-1-(-5))² + (-3-(-9))²) = √(4 + 16 + 36) = √56 = 2√14 ≈ 7.48 (3 sf). (b) Total surface area of a solid hemisphere = curved surface area + base area = ½(4πr²) + πr² = 3πr² = 3π(56) = 168π ≈ 528 (3 sf).

2. [Maximum mark: 6]

The following diagram shows a triangle ABC, with AB = 7, AC = 12 and BÂC = 116°.

diagram not to scale

[Triangle: vertex A at the left, vertex B at the top, vertex C at the right. Side AB is labelled 7, side AC is labelled 12. The angle at A (BÂC) is marked as 116°.]

(a) Find BC. [3]

(b) Find AĈB. [3]
questions.summary: Use cosine and sine rules to find side and angle in a triangle.
questions.solution: (a) Using the cosine rule, BC² = AB² + AC² − 2(AB)(AC)cos(BÂC) = 7² + 12² − 2(7)(12)cos116° = 266.646…, so BC = 16.3293… ≈ 16.3 (3 sf). (b) Using the sine rule, sin(AĈB)/7 = sin116°/16.3293…, so sin(AĈB) = 7sin116°/16.3293… = 0.385292…. Hence AĈB = 22.6619…° ≈ 22.7° (3 sf).

3. [Maximum mark: 5]

Consider the expansion of (x + k)¹¹, where k > 0.

(a) Write down the number of terms in the expansion. [1]

In the expansion, the coefficient of x⁷ is 1320.

(b) Find the value of k. [4]
questions.summary: Use binomial expansion to find the number of terms and solve for an unknown coefficient.
questions.solution: (a) The expansion has 12 terms. (b) In (x + k)¹¹ the general term is ¹¹Cᵣx¹¹⁻ʳkʳ. The term in x⁷ occurs when 11 − r = 7, so r = 4. Its coefficient is ¹¹C₄k⁴ = 330k⁴. Setting 330k⁴ = 1320 gives k⁴ = 4. Since k > 0, k = ⁴√4 = √2 ≈ 1.41 (3 sf).

questions.accessible_text:
4. [Maximum mark: 6]

A supermarket analyses the shopping habits of its customers.
The number of times, X, each customer visits the supermarket in a week is given by the following probability distribution.

[Table: The first row is headed x and contains 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, ≥ 6. The second row is headed P(X = x) and contains, respectively, 1.5a, 2a, 0.281, a, 0.026, 0.]

(a) (i) Find the value of a.
(ii) Write down the mode of X. [3]

(b) Find the mean of X. [2]

The manager wants to know why customers come to their supermarket. They survey the first 50 customers to arrive at the supermarket on a particular day.

(c) Identify which one of the following best describes the manager's sampling method. Circle your answer.

Simple random   /   Systematic   /   Convenience   /   Quota   /   Stratified [1]
questions.summary: Work with a discrete probability distribution, find mode and mean, and identify a sampling method.
questions.solution: (a)(i) Summing probabilities: 1.5a + 2a + 0.281 + a + 0.026 + 0 = 1, so 4.5a = 0.693, a = 0.154 (3 sf). (a)(ii) Mode is the value with highest probability: P(X=2) = 2a = 0.308, which is the largest, so mode = 2. (b) Mean = Σ x·P(X=x) = 1(1.5a) + 2(2a) + 3(0.281) + 4(a) + 5(0.026) = 1.5a + 4a + 0.843 + 4a + 0.13 = 9.5a + 0.973 = 9.5(0.154) + 0.973 = 1.463 + 0.973 = 2.436 ≈ 2.44 (3 sf). (c) Convenience (surveying the first 50 customers to arrive).

5. [Maximum mark: 5]

The following diagram shows a circle with centre O.
Points A, B and C lie on the circle.

diagram not to scale

[Circle with centre O. Points A, B, C are on the circumference. Angle AÔB = 2.51 radians is marked at the centre. Triangle AOB is drawn. The arc from A through C to B (the major arc ACB) is highlighted.]

The area of triangle AOB is 26 cm² and AÔB = 2.51 radians.

Find the length of arc ACB.
questions.summary: Find the radius from triangle area, then compute a major arc length.
questions.solution: Area of triangle AOB = ½ r² sin(AÔB) = 26, so ½ r² sin(2.51) = 26. sin(2.51) = 0.590803..., hence r² = 52 / 0.590803... = 88.0177..., r = 9.38462... cm. The major arc ACB subtends an angle of (2π − 2.51) = 3.77319... radians at the centre. Arc length = r × angle = 9.38462... × 3.77319... = 35.4035... ≈ 35.4 cm (3 sf).

6. [Maximum marks: 7]

Consider the function f(x) = (2x + a)³ / (x + 5)², where x ≠ -5 and a ∈ ℝ⁺.

(a) Find an expression for f′(x), in terms of a. [3]

When x = 1, the tangent to the graph of f makes an angle of 70° to the horizontal.

(b) Find the two possible values of a. [4]
questions.summary: Differentiate a rational function using quotient rule and solve for the parameter given the gradient.

7. [Maximum mark: 15]

Consider the function f(x) = (2/π) sin(3πx) + 2, where 0 ≤ x ≤ 2. The following diagram shows the graph of f.

[Graph of f for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2. x-axis from 0 to 2.5 labelled in steps of 0.5. y-axis from 0 to 3 labelled in steps of 0.5. The sinusoidal curve oscillates between y = 2 − 2/π ≈ 1.36 and y = 2 + 2/π ≈ 2.64, completing 3 full cycles from x = 0 to x = 2.]

(a) (i) Write down the amplitude of f.
(ii) Find the period of f. [3]

(b) The point P has coordinates (1.63, 2.16). State whether P lies above, below or on the graph of f. Justify your answer. [3]

The line L₁ has equation x − 6y + 11 = 0.

(c) Write down the gradient of the line L₁. [1]

The line L₁ is normal to the graph of f at point A(1, 2).
The line L₂ is tangent to the graph of f at A.

(d) (i) Find the gradient of L₂.
(ii) Hence, or otherwise, find the equation of L₂. [3]

The line L₁ intersects the graph of f at another point B, where the x-coordinate of B is greater than 1.5. This is shown in the following diagram.

[Diagram: Graph of f with line L₁ drawn through A(1,2) and point B. The region between A and B, bounded by the curve of f and the line L₁, is shaded.]

(e) Find the coordinates of B. [2]

The shaded region is enclosed by the graph of f and the line L₁ between A and B.

(f) Find the area of the shaded region. [3]
questions.summary: Analyze a sinusoidal function, its tangent and normal, intersection of curves, and area between them.
questions.solution: (a)(i) Amplitude = 2/π ≈ 0.637 (3 sf). (ii) Period = 2π / (3π) = 2/3 ≈ 0.667 (3 sf). (b) f(1.63) = (2/π) sin(3π × 1.63) + 2 = (2/π) sin(4.89π) + 2 = 2.21564... . Since 2.21564... > 2.16, f(1.63) > 2.16, so P lies below the graph of f. (c) x − 6y + 11 = 0 ⇒ 6y = x + 11 ⇒ y = (1/6)x + 11/6, gradient = 1/6 ≈ 0.167. (d)(i) L₁ is normal, so gradient of tangent L₂ = −1/(1/6) = −6. (d)(ii) Equation of L₂: y − 2 = −6(x − 1), i.e. y = −6x + 8, or 6x + y − 8 = 0. (e) Solve L₁ and f simultaneously: y = (x+11)/6 = (2/π) sin(3πx) + 2. Using GDC, intersection with x > 1.5 gives x = 1.64856..., y = 2.10809..., so B(1.65, 2.11) (3 sf). (f) Area = ∫₁^¹·⁶⁴⁸⁵⁶... [((x+11)/6) − ((2/π) sin(3πx) + 2)] dx = 0.253204... ≈ 0.253 (3 sf).

8. [Maximum mark: 17]

Consider a discrete random variable X.

(a) State two conditions required for X to be modelled by a binomial distribution. [2]

A water theme park has two rides: Daifong and Torbellino. Each visitor's decision to ride on either Daifong or Torbellino is made independently of any other person.
From previous records, it is expected that 37% of the visitors on any particular day will ride Daifong.
On Saturday, 1900 people will visit the theme park.

(b) Find the number of people that are expected to ride Daifong. [2]

(c) Find the probability that
(i) 712 people will ride Daifong;
(ii) between 684 and 712 people, inclusive, will ride Daifong. [4]

(d) Given that between 684 and 712 people, inclusive, will ride Daifong, find the probability that at most 692 people will ride Daifong. [4]

The ride Torbellino is more popular at the theme park. It is expected that 61% of the visitors on any particular day will ride Torbellino.
It can be assumed that the probability a person will ride Daifong is independent of them riding Torbellino.

(e) Find the probability that a person will ride both Daifong and Torbellino. [2]

Next Tuesday n people will visit the theme park. The probability that at most 500 people will ride Torbellino is approximately 0.693.

(f) Find the value of n. [3]
questions.summary: Apply binomial distribution to theme park visitor data, including conditional probability and independence.

9. [Maximum mark: 14]

Two athletes, Fiona and Lucy, compete in a 200 metres race along a straight track.
Fiona's velocity, in m s⁻¹, during the race can be modelled by v(t) = (8.14t) / √(t² + 0.2), where t ≥ 0.
Time, t, is measured in seconds from when the race starts.

(a) (i) Write down the value of v(1).
(ii) Find the time when Fiona's velocity is 5 m s⁻¹. [3]

(b) Find the time when Fiona's acceleration is 4 m s⁻². [2]

(c) (i) Write down the limit of v(t) as t approaches infinity.
(ii) State a reason why the value in part (c)(i) is not valid in the context of this question. [3]

Lucy's velocity, in m s⁻¹, during the race can be modelled by w(t) = (8t) / √(t² + 0.3), where t ≥ 0.

Fiona completes the race and crosses the finishing line in front of Lucy.

(d) Find the distance Lucy is from the finishing line when Fiona completes the 200 metres. [6]
questions.summary: Model a 200 m race using rational velocity functions, find times, limits, and Lucy's remaining distance.
